# Port the post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite hooks to the repo-root v2 wrappers

**Headline:** The three committed Worklog hooks are `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1`
wrappers that `exec` an absolute per-machine path,
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. When that path is absent (any
machine where `scripts/install_pi.sh` has not run), every checkout, merge and
`git worktree add` fails with `exec: … not found` (exit 127) and the post-pull
`wl sync` never runs — which broke `wl sync` in this repository on 2026-10-30
until `scripts/install_pi.sh` was re-run.

## Problem statement

`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` closed the "nothing creates the central script" half of
the problem by installing it from `install_pi.sh`. The remaining half is the
hard-coded absolute path itself: the hooks only work on a machine where the
installer ran, and a relocation or a fresh host silently disables the Worklog
sync. `ContentCreator` already migrated its hooks to `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2`
wrappers that resolve the delegate from the repository root
(`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) and fail open; this repository still ships the
v1 form.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** — `implement.py start/finish` and `wl sync` abort
  with exit 127 whenever git creates a worktree or checks out a branch on a
  machine without the central hook.
- **Developers on a fresh clone or a renamed checkout** — merges error on a
  hook they did not write and cannot see.
- **Producers** — Worklog data silently stops syncing when the hook errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
      `.githooks/post-rewrite` carry the `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2` marker,
      resolve `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`,
      `cd` there, and `exec` it.
- [ ] All three wrappers are fail-open: no resolvable repository root, a missing
      delegate, or a missing `wl`/`worklog` exits 0 so a merge or checkout never
      fails because of the hook.
- [ ] `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` still short-circuits the sync (delegate
      behaviour unchanged).
- [ ] Tests prove the hooks work with `$HOME` unset or pointing at a sandbox and
      without any `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, from the
      repository root and from a subdirectory, for all three wrappers.
- [ ] A test scans `.githooks/` and fails if any file regains a hard-coded
      absolute checkout path (the `ContentCreator` equivalent lives in
      `tests/test_worklog_hooks.py`).
- [ ] `scripts/install_pi.sh` no longer warns that the wrappers do not delegate
      to the central path, and either stops installing the central script or
      documents it as legacy.
- [ ] `docs/dev/` hook documentation describes the v2 wrappers and the fail-open
      contract.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `docs/dev/` hook pages.

## Constraints

- Keep `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as the single implementation of the
  post-pull sync; the wrappers stay thin.
- Do not change the pre-push hook or its gates.
- Removal of the central-script install from `install_pi.sh` is optional; if it
  stays, it must not be required for the hooks to work.

## Existing state

```
$ cat .githooks/post-checkout
#!/bin/sh
# worklog:post-pull-hook:v1
# Wrapper that delegates to central Worklog post-pull script (committed hooks).
exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

Observed failure (2026-10-30, `wl sync` in this repository):

```
✗ Sync failed: Command failed with exit code 127: git worktree add --detach '…/.worklog/tmp-worktree-yZC0Kd/wt' 'refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data'
Preparing worktree (detached HEAD a07575c13)
/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
```

Running `scripts/install_pi.sh` created
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` and the sync then succeeded — a
workaround, not a fix.

## Desired change

Replace the three v1 wrappers with the v2 wrapper (see
`ContentCreator/.githooks/post-merge` for the canonical text), extend
`tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` (or a new hook test module) with the
`$HOME`-independent cases, and update `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the docs to
match.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-merge` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-rewrite` — v2 wrapper
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — hook behaviour without the central
  script; hard-coded-path scan
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — stop requiring the central script; drop the
  delegation warning
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (or the equivalent hook page) — v2 wrapper
  contract

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` works when executed from the
  repository root; that is how `post-merge` already invokes it.
- **Risk (low):** a `post-checkout` run inside `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (the
  Worklog data branch) would sync from that temporary checkout. Mitigation: the
  delegate is already fail-open and warns on failure; verify it does not
  recurse when the temporary worktree has no `.worklog`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** consolidating the hooks with the ContentCreator copy
  into one shared installer is tempting. Record that separately; this item only
  ports the v2 wrapper shape.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — installs the central post-pull script (the other half
  of the same failure mode).
- `SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX` — fail-open portability warning added to
  `install_pi.sh`.
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` (ContentCreator) — the item whose `wl sync` surfaced
  this failure.
data.title: Port the post-checkout/post-merge/post-rewrite hooks to the repo-root v2 wrappers

data.description:
# Intake: Only mark as complete when fully complete

The implement skill transitions a work item to `completed`/`in_review` and releases its assignee hold before the implement run has finished every step, leaving a window in which the herdr downtime dispatcher picks the item up and dispatches an audit that races the still-running implement session.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` issues the terminal `status=completed` / `stage=in_review` write (and, by default, clears the assignee hold) inside its `StatusLifecycle` block, then returns. The implement session still has work to do afterwards — worktree cleanup, the commit-hash completion comment, and the belt-and-suspenders read-only **post-push full-suite verification** (which the SKILL.md explicitly describes as running "post-push, post-`in_review`"). Once the assignee is cleared and the item is `in_review`, the item is a valid audit candidate: `selectAuditCandidate` in the herdr downtime worker excludes only soft-deleted, fresh-audit, child, producer-review, and **assignee-held** items. The dispatcher can therefore dispatch an audit while the implement session is still verifying/cleaning up, producing duplicate or conflicting work and audit records for an item whose implement run has not actually finished.

## Users

- **Implementing agent** — "As an agent running `/skill:implement`, I want the item to stay out of the audit queue until I have finished every step, so an audit never races my post-push verification."
  - Example: leaf item finishes build/test/commit/push; while the session runs its post-push full-suite verification, the downtime dispatcher must not claim the item for audit.
- **Downtime dispatcher / audit operator** — "As the audit dispatcher, I want to see an item as audit-ready only when the implement run is genuinely over, so I never audit a half-finished lifecycle."
- **Release manager** — "As a release manager, I want `in_review` to mean 'implementation fully finished and ready for audit', not 'finish sub-command returned'."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No premature terminal transition.** The implement skill must not make an item observable as `completed`/`in_review` with a cleared assignee while any implement-run step remains to be performed. Concretely: while the session is still doing post-push verification, worktree cleanup, or the completion comment, the item is either still `in_progress` with the assignee held, or otherwise excluded from audit dispatch by an explicit, documented hold. The terminal transition and assignee release happen only as the implement run's last lifecycle action.
2. **Observable audit-dispatch hold.** A regression test proves that during the post-push phase the item is not a valid audit candidate (non-empty assignee and/or non-`in_review` state), and that it becomes a valid candidate only after the final lifecycle step. The test exercises the real `implement.py` state machine (not a re-implementation) and asserts the transition ordering.
3. **Recoverable interruption.** An implement run interrupted before its final step leaves the item in a non-terminal, non-audit-ready state (`in_progress`/`open`) with the held assignee cleared or reclaimable, plus a comment/read-back that names the retained state — never stuck permanently in `completed`/`in_review` for work that did not finish. Existing abort/safety-reset paths keep passing their tests.
4. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.** Specifically: `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (Step 9 / status-transition matrix), `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, and the affected code comments describe the finalisation ordering and the hold/transition contract. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (ship pipeline owns it).
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes**, including the new regression test(s) and all existing implement/status-lifecycle tests.

## Constraints

- **Do not change the herdr/ContextHub downtime dispatcher** as the primary fix: the invariant belongs to the implement skill, which owns the lifecycle transition. (A dispatcher change would only be a fallback if the skill cannot express the hold; note it as a linked item if needed.)
- **Preserve the assignee-hold convention** (non-empty assignee = scheduling hold; clear to release) and `StatusLifecycle` semantics — the fix must not leave finished items permanently held (SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH / SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL regressions).
- **Preserve the terminal-status read-back guarantee** (`_assert_terminal_status`, OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): after the run is genuinely finished the store must hold `completed`/`in_review`, and a lost write must still fail loudly.
- **Preserve idempotence/recovery**: re-running `finish` after an interruption must converge; an interrupted run must never strand a worktree or a held item.
- Work must be done in the implement worktree via `implement.py start` (worktree isolation), with build → test → commit ordering.
- UK English in all written output.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `phase_finish()` wraps steps 3d–7 in `with StatusLifecycle(work_item_id, assignee=..., target_stage="in_review")` (~line 7367). On normal exit `StatusLifecycle.__exit__` writes `status=completed` + `stage=in_review` and releases the assignee (release is the helper default). `_assert_terminal_status()` (~line 7662) reads the store back afterwards.
  - `phase_parent()` advances a parent to `completed`/`in_review` once all children are terminal (~line 8516); `_finalise_stranded_child()` does the same for a driven stranded child (~line 9679).
  - The manual completion comment and post-push verification are not part of `finish`; they are instructed by `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9 *after* `finish` returns.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `StatusLifecycle` sets `in_progress` on entry, `completed` (+ optional stage) and releases the assignee on success; restores on exception.
- ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `selectAuditCandidate` filters `completed/in_review` items by soft-delete, audit freshness, `parentId`, `needsProducerReview`, **`isAssigneeHeld`**, and a 7-day recency window. `isAssigneeHeld` is the only hold the implement skill can currently exercise, and `finish` clears it.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9 — "Read-only post-push verification (belt-and-suspenders, post-push, post-`in_review`)" is the concrete race window.

## Desired change

Make the implement run's terminal lifecycle write (and the assignee release that makes the item dispatchable) the **last** action of the run. Candidate designs — the implement phase may choose, but the chosen design must satisfy every AC:

- **(A) Verify-then-transition:** move the post-push verification (and any other required post-push work) into `phase_finish` before the `StatusLifecycle` exit, so `finish` returns only when the run is fully complete.
- **(B) Two-phase finish:** `finish` performs build/test/commit/push/cleanup but keeps the item `in_progress` with the assignee held; a final `implement.py complete` (or `finish --finalise`) performs the terminal transition after verification. The SKILL.md invokes it as the last step.
- **(C) Session-active hold:** keep the assignee hold until the session's final step, with a documented, bounded stale-hold reclamation for crashed sessions.

Whichever design is chosen, the outcome is: **no `completed`/`in_review` + empty-assignee window while the implement run still has steps to run**, and an interrupted run leaves a recoverable non-terminal state.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` transition ordering, `_assert_terminal_status` placement, new finalise/complete action (if design B), abort/safety-reset paths.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — new regression test proving the audit-dispatch hold ordering; update existing finish/status tests (`test_finish_no_diff_status.py`, finish-harness tests).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the hold/deferred-transition contract needs a helper (e.g. a session-active hold); avoid changing default release semantics.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Step 9 ordering, post-push verification position, status-transition matrix.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — document the finalisation ordering and the audit-dispatch hold contract.
- `docs/dev/status-lifecycle-reference.md` (if present) / `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py` — pin the unchanged release semantics.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL** — Flip StatusLifecycle assignee-release default (completed). The release default is what makes the item dispatchable the moment `finish` exits; the fix must not regress it.
- **SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH** — Enforce assignee release on every terminal outcome across all skills (in progress, plan_complete). Bounds the "hold until final step" design so finished items are never left held.
- **SA-0MV85WCJJ0087VMP** — herdr: exclude assignee-held items from audit candidates (completed). This is the hold mechanism the implement skill can use.
- **SA-0MS6B5ESG0056GZJ** — Prevent unintended stage advancement to `done` outside ship (completed). Adjacent lifecycle-transition safety precedent.
- **SA-0MVI35BIU002MTZQ** — Audit runner: parent-persisted child audits demote in_review children (completed). Adjacent "audit raced a lifecycle transition" precedent and its regression-test style.
- **SA-0MVME1PI5005WU58 / OSL-0MVMB44C9008IXZX** — terminal-status read-back guarantee on both finish paths; the fix must preserve it.
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** — audit staleness race: post-persist comment bumps `updatedAt` past `auditedAt` (completed). Adjacent "post-audit comment ordering" race precedent.
- `docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md` — describes the downtime dispatcher's strict idle gate and audit-dispatch behaviour.
- ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `selectAuditCandidate` / `isAssigneeHeld` (external repo, reference only).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: a hold that outlives the run blocks dispatch forever.** Mitigation: bounded stale-hold reclamation and AC3's recoverable-interruption test; do not weaken `SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH`.
- **Risk: moving the full-suite verification into `finish` adds latency.** Mitigation: the verification is read-only against the dev-push cache; design A only re-orders, it does not add a suite run.
- **Risk: a two-phase finish leaves the item `in_progress` if a session dies between `finish` and `complete`.** Mitigation: `open`/`in_progress` is recoverable by design (no audit dispatch), and the existing abort/safety-reset paths already reset to `open`.
- **Risk: scope creep** into redesigning the dispatcher. Mitigation: keep the fix in the implement skill; file dispatcher changes as linked work items.
- **Assumption:** "fully complete" means the entire implement run, including the SKILL.md Step 9 post-push verification, worktree cleanup, and completion comment — i.e. the session's last lifecycle action. (Confirmed by the item description "before it has completed its run".)
- **Assumption:** the downtime dispatcher's `isAssigneeHeld` filter is the intended hold mechanism in this repo's contract; no ContextHub change is required for the primary fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (item title and description) plus repository inspection identified the concrete race window (`finish` transitions and releases the assignee before Step 9's post-push verification/cleanup) and the dispatcher's `isAssigneeHeld` filter. Two assumptions are recorded in **Risks and assumptions** above and are flagged for producer confirmation in the completion summary.

- Q: "What counts as 'fully complete'?" — Answer (derived from item description, no interaction): the entire implement run, including post-push verification, worktree cleanup and the completion comment; the terminal write must be the run's last lifecycle action. Source: item description + `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9.
- Q: "Is the dispatcher in scope?" — Answer (agent inference, flagged as assumption): no — the fix belongs in the implement skill, which owns the transition. Source: repo boundaries (`AGENTS.md` coding discipline 4) and the dispatcher living in ContextHub.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQ01FDQ5003H09A** – Implementation: update AMPA audit handlers to use wl audit-set (completed)
- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** – Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit (blocked)

# `test_guarded_run_all.py` fails when the finish gate exports `GIT_INDEX_FILE`

## Goal

Make `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` hermetic under the finish
gate, so a change that selects this file in changed scope can pass the gate.

**Headline:** the finish gate exports a temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE` for the
whole suite (SA-0MVQHVGFR006W8LG) and it deliberately survives the test
skill's repository-override scrub (SA-0MVQHV9Y3001RNNW). Tests in
`test_guarded_run_all.py` spawn *helper subprocesses* whose `git add -A` /
`git commit` then write into the **gate's** index instead of the fixture
repo's own index, so the fixture's working tree still shows the file as
untracked (`??`) and the guard reports a `live_repo_mutation`.

## Evidence (reproduced while implementing SA-0MVQQ9HXV000V6Z4)

Command (simulating the gate's exported index):

```bash
cp <worktree-git-dir>/index /tmp/gate.index
GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/gate.index git -C <worktree> add -A
GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/gate.index python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py \
  --group test --json
```

Result: `2 failed, 181 passed` —

- `test_guarded_run_all.py::test_guarded_run_fast_forward_of_main_checkout_dev_is_expected_churn`
  → `live-repo mutation detected … added path [??] shared.txt`
- `test_guarded_run_all.py::test_guarded_run_reports_excluded_churn_without_failing`

Both pass outside the gate (no ambient `GIT_INDEX_FILE`), which is why the
bug is invisible until the file is in a gate's changed scope.

## Root cause

A foreign index in `GIT_INDEX_FILE` makes `git` in *another* repository treat
every tracked path as changed (`git diff <commit>`) and makes
`git add -A`/`git commit` write into that foreign index. The two tests run
their "concurrent actor"/fast-forward script as a child process that inherits
the full environment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Hermetic helper subprocesses.** The helper scripts spawned by
  `test_guarded_run_all.py` run with a hermetic git environment
  (`shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()` or an explicit
  `env={"GIT_INDEX_FILE": …}`), so their git commands target their own repo.
- [ ] **AC2 — Green under a gate-like environment.** `--group test` passes with
  a foreign `GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported (the reproduction above): 0 failures.
- [ ] **AC3 — Unchanged outside the gate.** The same tests stay green in a
  normal full-suite run, with no behavioural change to the guard.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (`fixture_git_env`)

## Related work

- `discovered-from:SA-0MVQQ9HXV000V6Z4` — found while adding the F0 baseline
  regression tests; the same class of bug was fixed in
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` there (autouse hermetic
  `GIT_INDEX_FILE` fixture).
- SA-0MVQHV9Y3001RNNW — pins that `GIT_INDEX_FILE` survives the scrub.
- SA-0MVQHVGFR006W8LG — the finish gate's temporary index.

# Finish main-checkout guard: verify on failure paths and never attribute/act on another checkout

**Discovered from:** WL-0MVWK20DK004TQZM (ContextHub, critical) — the 2026-10-31 recurrence of `packages/shared` being wiped from the main checkout. Producer decision (Option C, 2026-10-31): the `implement.py` guard changes ship here; the ContextHub item keeps forensics, the wl diagnostic, recovery runbook/script and a ContextHub-side integrity check, and both items cross-reference.

## Problem

The finish main-checkout guard shipped in v1.0.24 (WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG) did not prevent a second wipe of `packages/shared` from the main ContextHub checkout on 2026-10-31, and did not report it. Two coverage gaps:

1. **Failure-path gap.** The guard snapshots at finish start and verifies only at pre-push and pre-worktree-removal (`verifies` array). The 2026-10-31 run aborted at the test gate (`.worklog/logs/finish-child4d.log`: `snapshot_at` 14:43:06, `verifies: []`) before any verify point, so 37 deletions in the main checkout were never evaluated or reported by any guard.
2. **Cross-checkout attribution gap.** A concurrent AI_Hell finish reported, in its `own_churn`, seven paths belonging to other work items (`docs/Game Design Document.md`, five `src/powerups/*`, `src/vfx/droneFeel.docs.test.ts`) while its own main checkout stayed clean — the guard's attribution (`_record_finish_own_churn` = `git diff --name-only before/after HEAD` on `repo_root`) can apparently pull paths from outside the repo being finished. The write surfaces of the guard and `wl_cleanup_worktree` need a read-only audit.

## Users

- **AI implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` from a linked worktree on a shared main checkout. User story: *As an implementation agent, I want a failed finish to tell me loudly that another actor mutated the main checkout, naming every path, so that I never silently build on, fast-forward over or push foreign deletions.*
- **The producer/operator** supervising several concurrent agents on one host. User story: *As the producer, I want finish's attribution to name only paths from the repo being finished, so a clean run cannot be blamed for another checkout's churn and a foreign deletion cannot be attributed to — or "fixed" by — the wrong run.*

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Failure-path verification.** When finish aborts before the push (gate failure, build failure, refactor failure, user abort) and the main-checkout snapshot shows foreign changes (deletions especially), the guard reports them loudly — naming every path and the concurrent-actor evidence — via a wl comment on the work item, leaving the item open. A regression test covers a foreign-deletion abort at the gate stage (`verifies` non-empty on failure paths).
2. **Cross-checkout safety.** A command run inside one checkout (worktree or repo) can never delete or modify tracked files in another reachable checkout, including a sibling repository outside the one being finished. Regression test proves an attempted deletion from a worktree-scoped run leaves the sibling checkout untouched and fails loudly.
3. **Attribution correctness.** `own_churn` never lists paths belonging to another checkout/repo, and the guard's `repo_root` resolution can never resolve to, or act on, a path outside its own repo. A test asserts foreign paths are not allow-listed and are reported as violations instead.
4. **Read-only audit.** The guard's and `wl_cleanup_worktree`'s write surfaces are verified read-only with respect to anything outside `repo_root`/the own worktree; findings recorded in this item.
5. **No regression on benign concurrent churn.** All changed-scope tests pass; the finish gate stays green for a clean run (no false positives on benign concurrent churn — the SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG defect class must not regress).
6. **Testing and validation.** Each of AC1–AC3 ships with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix tree and passes on the fixed tree, exercising production code (no self-referential simulations).
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not regress SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG: benign working-tree churn attributable to a concurrent session must still be excluded from the guard verdict (and surfaced as a note), not turned into a false-positive abort.
- All implementation happens in the `implement.py start` worktree; never edit, commit or push from the main checkout. Finish's own Step-5 fast-forward churn remains allow-listed (deletions are never allow-listed).
- Build → test → commit ordering; only push to `dev`, never `main`.
- The guard is a safety net, not a concurrency lock: cross-repo concurrency is out of the existing per-repo finish lock's scope (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84).
- Fail loud, never silent: a foreign mutation must produce an auditable wl comment even when the status is reset to `open`.

## Existing state

- `_snapshot_main_checkout` captures a `{path: porcelain-code}` map (excluding `.worklog/`) at finish start (`main_checkout_guard["snapshot_at"]`).
- `_verify_main_checkout` re-snapshots and appends `{stage, at, verdict, offending?, actor_evidence?}` to `guard["verifies"]`; it is called only from `_abort_on_main_checkout_violation` at **pre-push** and **pre-worktree-removal**. Build failure, gate failure and user abort return early before either verify point, so `verifies: []` on those paths.
- `_main_checkout_guard_violations` classifies a changed path as offending unless it is under `.worklog/`, project expected-dirty, or in `own_churn` with a non-deletion code.
- `_record_finish_own_churn(repo_root, before_head, after_head)` runs `git diff --name-only` on `repo_root`; `_resolve_main_repo_root` trusts `state.repo_root` unless it resolves to/inside the worktree, then derives from `worktree_path` via `_get_repo_root`.
- `_main_checkout_actor_evidence` scans other `.implement_state.json` files and `/proc/<pid>/cwd` for concurrent-actor evidence.
- `wl_cleanup_worktree` and the finish write surfaces (fast-forward, push, worktree removal) need a documented read-only audit against paths outside `repo_root`/the own worktree.

## Desired change

1. **Add failure-path verify points.** Run the guard verify on every finish abort path before the push (build failure, gate failure after retries, refactor failure, interactive user abort), so `verifies` is non-empty on failure and foreign deletions are reported via a wl comment, leaving the item `open`.
2. **Harden attribution and `repo_root`.** Constrain `own_churn`/attribution to the repo being finished and make `_resolve_main_repo_root` fail closed (or refuse loudly) when it would resolve outside its own repo, so foreign paths can never be allow-listed or attributed. Prove with a test that foreign paths are reported as violations, never allow-listed.
3. **Audit write surfaces.** Document, in this item, that the guard and `wl_cleanup_worktree` write only within `repo_root`/the own worktree; fix any surface that does not.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish main-checkout guard: `_snapshot_main_checkout`, `_verify_main_checkout`, `_main_checkout_guard_violations`, `_record_finish_own_churn`, `_main_checkout_actor_evidence`, `_resolve_main_repo_root`, `wl_cleanup_worktree`; verify-point wiring in `phase_finish` (failure paths in Steps 1–3).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py` — add failure-path (gate/build/user-abort) and cross-checkout attribution regression tests.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — live-repo guard precedent for attribution allow-lists / churn exclusion.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` — finish-lock tests (cross-repo scope note).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — document the guard's verify points, failure-path reporting and attribution contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **False positives (highest risk).** Adding verify points on failure paths can abort a legitimately failing run for benign churn. Mitigation: reuse the existing allow-list (`own_churn` non-deletion, `.worklog/`, expected-dirty) and keep SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG's concurrent-churn exclusion; add a clean-run regression test.
- **Deletion vs modification.** A fast-forward cannot delete a file relative to the tracked tree, so `D` entries are treated as foreign by construction; hardening attribution must preserve this invariant.
- **Cross-repo reachability.** The `repo_root` resolution can be given a sibling checkout; fail-closed resolution plus a real-repo sibling test is the safety net.
- **Assumption:** the 2026-10-31 log evidence (`snapshot_at` 14:43:06, `verifies: []`, 37 deletions) is accurate and reproducible via a gate-stage abort harness.
- **Assumption:** `wl_cleanup_worktree` and the other finish write surfaces are intended to act only on `repo_root`/the own worktree; the audit records evidence, and any deviation is fixed, not documented away.
- **Scope-creep control:** broader cross-repo locking, recovery tooling and the ContextHub-side integrity check belong to WL-0MVWK20DK004TQZM and are explicitly out of scope here.

## Related work

- SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG — live-repo guard false positives on concurrent churn (completed) — attribution/allow-list precedent; must not regress.
- SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN — push from the worktree holding the commit (blocked) — Step-5 fast-forward + pre-push guard interplay.
- WL-0MVPE2CMW006K25Q — finish aborts loudly on foreign main-checkout deletions (ContextHub, completed) — the existing fail-loud deletion guard.
- WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84 — single-owner finish lock (ContextHub, completed) — per-repo only; cross-repo concurrency is out of that lock's scope.
- WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET — finish fast-forwards main dev mid-test-run (open) — gate-window concurrency.
- WL-0MVWK20DK004TQZM — parent ContextHub item (intake_complete; owns forensics/diagnostic/recovery + ContextHub-side integrity check).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (parent forensics, the 2026-10-31 log evidence, the producer's Option C decision and the listed AC2/AC3 scope) was sufficient to draft the brief. The item was created as a `bug` because it corrects incorrect/broken guard behaviour (missed failure-path detection and cross-checkout attribution), and priority `high` because it is an important, blocking-class safety defect.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V** – Unify test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout (open)
- **SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2** – Enforce git worktree usage for all implementation work (completed)
- **SA-0MV87GDRY001GKH2** – Document ownership rule and .worklog churn scope (completed)

# GitHub closes the idle SSH connection during the pre-push full-suite gate

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** — this is the concrete root cause behind one of the
"transient push-transport closes" that item asks us to retry. Retrying does not
help on its own: the connection is dropped with a *deterministic* trigger
(SSH idling for the duration of the suite), so every attempt fails the same way
and the agent loops, burning a full suite run each time.

## Problem

`.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full` **after** `git` has
established the SSH connection to `github.com` and **before** the ref update.
The hook produces no SSH traffic for the whole run (measured 11 min warm, 35 min
cold on this host), so the remote closes the idle connection:

```
pre-push: full-suite gate for dev/main push — running run_tests.py --scope full ...
Connection to github.com closed by remote host.
pre-push: full suite green (cached runs make repeat pushes cheap)
pre-push: mirrored gate cache entry 96dd15da... into .worklog/cache
```

The gate reports **green**, the cache entries are mirrored — and the push never
lands: `git push` exits without updating the ref and `origin/dev` is unchanged.
Observed 2026-10-31 on two consecutive attempts from
`wl-LP-0MVWIA33O004RKP7-…` in `llm-manager`; `~/.ssh/config` sets no
`ServerAliveInterval`/`TCPKeepAlive`.

Impact:

- A green full-suite run is discarded, so the most expensive part of the push is
  paid repeatedly; because each retry rebases onto a moved `dev`, the tree
  changes and the suite cache misses, so retries are *cold*.
- The output reads as success ("full suite green") while the push silently did
  not happen — the misleading signal is arguably worse than a hard failure.

## Workaround that worked (not a fix)

```bash
GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20 -o TCPKeepAlive=yes" \
  WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev
# -> d925d89d..877a6512  HEAD -> dev
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dev push whose pre-push gate runs longer than the remote's idle timeout
      succeeds, with no manual `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` override by the agent.
- [ ] Keepalives are configured in a way that survives a fresh clone/worktree
      (e.g. set by the hook or by `implement.py`'s push, not only in one
      operator's `~/.ssh/config`).
- [ ] When the ref update is still lost after a green suite, the push reports a
      distinct, loud failure (not "full suite green" followed by silence), and
      distinguishes "suite red" from "transport lost".
- [ ] A regression test covers the transport-loss path (simulated closed
      connection) and asserts the distinct failure classification.

## Notes

- `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` / `SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN` (push must run from the worktree)
  is a separate defect; both were hit in the same session. This item is only the
  transport side.
- Related: `~/.ssh/config` on the multi-agent host currently has no
  `ServerAlive*` settings at all.
data.title: GitHub closes the idle SSH connection during the pre-push full-suite gate, silently discarding a green gate

# implement.py Key Files gate misses the bold-inside-heading form

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-31). That RISE item was filed during `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` and is deleted once this item exists (producer decision Q1 = re-file here).

**Headline:** The Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate in `implement.py` parses only
`## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)` and a bare `**Key Files:**` line, so a
work item whose section is written `## **Key Files:**` (bold marker nested in an
H2/H3) yields no key files, dirty-file relevance becomes unjudgeable, and
`implement.py start` aborts on a dirty checkout even when every dirty path is
unrelated. Make the heading matcher form-agnostic and lock it down with
regression tests.

## Problem statement

`_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` matches
`#{1,6}\s*Key Files.*` (heading) **or** `\*\*Key Files:?\*\*.*` (bold line) — but
not the combination `## **Key Files:**`, because after the `## ` prefix the next
token is `**`, not `Key Files`. `extract_key_files_from_description()` then
returns `[]`, `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` reports *"no Key Files section in
the work item description — cannot judge dirty-file relevance"*, and
`phase_start` takes the conservative abort-and-ask branch even though the
description does list key files and the dirty paths demonstrably do not overlap
them. The gate's conservative default is correct; it is being tripped by a
parser gap rather than by a real risk.

## Evidence

Reproduced in this session against the installed skill tree
(`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`):

| form | `extract_key_files_from_description` |
|---|---|
| `## Key Files` | `['a/b.ts', 'tests/c.test.ts']` |
| `## Key Files (predicted)` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `**Key Files:**` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `## **Key Files:**` | `[]` |
| `### **Key Files:**` | `[]` |

- **Corpus prevalence (consumer store):** 9 of 386 items in the
  `tce-the-rising` store use the bold-inside-heading form — the face-off tie
  epic parent RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU and its eight children
  (RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX, RISE-0MVRMI7GR006QH44, RISE-0MVRMI9F0007HXBW,
  RISE-0MVRMIB7Z008P1HB, RISE-0MVRMID1B0098HAY, RISE-0MVRMIF0T008A72W,
  RISE-0MVRMIGXS0073HDX, RISE-0MVRMIISC009TXYX). For comparison: 297 items use
  a plain heading, 52 a bare bold line, 28 none.
- **Observed stall:** `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` aborted on child
  RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX (Key Files: `tests/the-rising/risingMatchHarness.ts`,
  `tests/the-rising/TheRisingRules.test.ts`) although the only dirty paths were
  six untracked `standups/*.md` files — zero overlap, i.e. exactly the
  documented "proceed, leave the dirty files untouched" case. The operator
  worked around it by pre-creating the worktree and running `start` from inside
  it (where the main-checkout gate is skipped by design).
- **No direct test coverage** of `extract_key_files_from_description`,
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files` or `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` exists under
  `skill/implement/tests/`, so this class of gap is invisible to the suite.
- The framework does **not** emit the H2-wrapped form itself:
  `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` (`_parse_key_files_section`,
  `validate_key_files_format`) and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` use a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line, so both families of form must keep working.

## Users

- **Implement-skill agent (primary)**: "When I start an item whose Key Files
  section is written `## **Key Files:**`, I want `start` to read those paths and
  let me proceed when the dirty files are unrelated, so I do not have to
  hand-work around a gate that already has the information it needs."
- **Producer / operator (secondary)**: "When a downtime run dispatches a child
  session, I want `start` to proceed or abort for a real reason, so unattended
  runs do not stall on a parsing bug."
- **Framework maintainer**: "I want every accepted Key Files heading form
  covered by a table-driven test, so a future edit to the extractor cannot
  silently drop a form."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `extract_key_files_from_description()` returns the listed paths for
  any `Key Files` heading regardless of emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or
  case: `## **Key Files:**`, `### **Key Files:**`, `## **Key Files (predicted):**`,
  `#### key files`, asserted by a table-driven unit test in
  `skill/implement/tests/`.
- **AC2** — Every currently supported form keeps working, asserted in the same
  table: `## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)`, `### Key Files`, and a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line; plus the tolerant bare-marker variants —
  `  **Key Files:**` (indented/whitespace) and `**Key Files**` (no colon).
- **AC3** — `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` proceeds (`can_proceed: true`)
  when the description uses `## **Key Files:**` and the dirty paths do not
  overlap those entries, and still aborts (`can_proceed: false`) when a dirty
  path does overlap, or when the description has no Key Files section at all.
- **AC4** — Extraction still stops at the end of the Key Files section: a
  following `#`/`##`/`###` heading or standalone bold section marker terminates
  the list, so prose lines and acceptance-criteria bullets never leak in as
  paths (regression guard for the SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2 defect class).
- **AC5** — A regression test demonstrates the defect before the fix (red on the
  current implementation, green after), and the end-to-end path is verified:
  `implement.py start` on a `## **Key Files:**` item with only unrelated dirty
  paths creates the worktree, leaves the dirty files untouched and records the
  decision in a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — The gate's safety properties are preserved: no
  stash/commit/revert of dirty files, and abort-and-ask still fires for "no Key
  Files section" and for any overlap.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments and docstrings in `implement.py` and the accepted-forms
  list in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree
  gate, SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR) plus the project README and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`** plus its tests and docs
  (producer decision Q2 = A). The two sibling parsers — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — are fixed by linked follow-up
  items (below), not here.
- **The gate stays conservative.** No Key Files section, or any overlapping
  dirty path, must still abort and ask. Nothing here may turn the gate into a
  whitelist or relax "never stash/commit/revert the user's work".
- **Must not regress existing forms.** The new matcher may be more tolerant but
  never stricter: an item that starts cleanly today must still start cleanly.
- **Minimal surface.** No new configuration knob or environment variable.
- **UK English** in comments, docstrings and docs.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` (~line 1671),
  `extract_key_files_from_description()` (~1676),
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files()` (~1712), `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()`
  (~1742), and the `phase_start` call site (~5993) that turns a
  `can_proceed: false` verdict into the dirty-worktree abort.
- The extractor's loop already terminates on a `#`-heading line or a non-bullet
  line starting with `**`; only the initial heading match is wrong. A new
  matcher must not let the matched heading's own bold marker look like the
  section end.
- `skill/implement/tests/` has suites for the start/finish gates but none that
  exercises the Key Files extractor or the relevance classifier.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate
  section) enumerates the three supported forms and needs the tolerant list.

## Desired change

1. Replace the two-branch heading regex with one form-agnostic matcher: an
   optional H1–H6 prefix, an optional `**` bold marker, `Key Files`, an optional
   parenthetical qualifier and optional closing `**`/`:`, matched
   case-insensitively — while still requiring `Key Files` to be the first
   content token (so `## Notes on Key Files` stays unmatched unless it matches
   today).
2. Keep the section terminator and the bullet/backtick path parsing unchanged
   (including `path → note`).
3. Add the table-driven tests (AC1–AC5) and the end-to-end `start` regression.
4. Update the docstring/comment and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — form-agnostic `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE`,
  extractor terminator/docstrings; classifier branches unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_key_files_extraction.py` — new table-driven tests
  for the accepted forms, the terminator behaviour and
  `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` proceed/abort decisions.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — accepted-forms list in the
  Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate section.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — over/under-matching:** tightening "first content token" could make a
  heading that matches today (e.g. `## Key Files and notes`) stop matching.
  Keep the match at least as wide as today; assert the old forms in the table.
- **Risk — terminator drift:** after accepting the new form the loop must not
  treat the matched heading's own `**` as a section end.
- **Risk — untestable "it works now" claims:** the AC5 end-to-end check needs a
  deliberately dirty main checkout, so it must leave the dirty files untouched
  and clean up after itself (or exercise the classifier/`phase_start` seam
  directly).
- **Assumption:** the H2-wrapped form is agent-authored markdown, not framework
  output — so the fix belongs in the tolerant parser, not in the plan skill's
  emitter.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the plan/audit parsers are separate items (below);
  anything further discovered goes to `discovered-from` items, not this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR** — Allow implement.py start to create a clean worktree
  when main checkout is dirty: introduced the gate and the three-form parser;
  this item fixes its blind spot.
- **SA-0MUYEV5AO006V0HK** — project-local skill extensions / dirty-tree
  exemptions (the other documented relaxation path of the same gate).
- **SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2** — `plan_helpers._parse_key_files_section` did not stop
  at Markdown headings (same failure family: section-boundary parsing).
- **SA-0MTYP6T2I00396J7** — generated `standups/` output not gitignored: the
  source of the six dirty files in the reproduction.
- **SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ** — the previous framework fix discovered from a
  tce-the-rising implement run (disposition precedent for this re-filing).
- **RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU** — Face-off tie epic whose children carry the
  `## **Key Files:**` form and whose drive run hit the abort.

## Linked follow-up items (producer decision Q2 = B and C)

- **Follow-up 1 — plan parser:** `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  `_parse_key_files_section` / `validate_key_files_format` should accept the same
  heading forms so plan validation does not report a missing/empty Key Files
  section for a validly-written description.
- **Follow-up 2 — audit parser:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`'s Key
  Files extraction (`^#{0,4}\s*Key Files.*?$`) has the same blind spot, which
  omits the item's files from the Phase 2 file-scope manifest. Either fix it
  locally or extract one shared, heading-aware Key Files helper consumed by
  implement/plan/audit.

Both are filed with `discovered-from:<this item>`; their SA ids are recorded in
this item's comments.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

Interview raised on RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (comment `RISE-C0MVWO1N400000N41`),
answered by the producer in-session on 2026-10-31. Answers are transcribed
verbatim.

- **Q1 — Which worklog/store carries the fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A - delete this when filed"** → the fix is re-filed in
  the SorraAgents worklog as this item (with `discovered-from:RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8`)
  and the RISE item is deleted once this item exists. Recommended option A was
  accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q2 — How wide is the parser fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A, with B and C as linked follow-ups"** →
  `implement.py` only in this item; the plan parser (B) and audit parser (C) are
  filed as linked follow-up items rather than folded in. Recommended option A
  was accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q3 — Which heading variants must be accepted?**
  **Answer (producer): "B + C"** → accept any `Key Files` heading regardless of
  emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or case (B), **and** tolerate whitespace /
  colon variants of the bare bold marker (C). Recommended option was B; the
  producer widened it to B+C, reflected in AC1/AC2. Source: interactive reply,
  this session.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — Does the framework emit the
  H2-wrapped form?** No: `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py:127-160` and
  `skill/plan/SKILL.md:181,306` specify a bare `**Key Files:**` line; the
  H2-wrapped form in the consumer store was authored into descriptions directly.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — How many items are affected in the
  consumer store?** 9 of 386 (`tce-the-rising`), all inside the face-off tie
  epic. Evidence: SQL scan of that store's `workitems.description`.

# Fixture git helpers across `tests/` must be hermetic under the finish gate's inherited `GIT_INDEX_FILE`

Discovered-from: **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (epic), during the child
SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D finish gate.

## Problem

The finish gate exports a temporary would-be-commit index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`,
SA-0MVQHVGFR006W8LG) for the suite it runs, and that variable deliberately
survives the repository-override scrub (F3, SA-0MVQHV9Y3001RNNW). Any test
fixture that runs raw `git init/add/commit` in its own throwaway repository
therefore writes into the **gate's** index. The gate then reports

> gate evidence invalid: the temporary index changed while the suite ran …
> Fixture git commands must use a hermetic environment

and refuses the verdict, so `implement.py finish` fails with
`reason: infrastructure` for any change whose changed scope includes such a
fixture — regardless of the change under test.

Measured on 2026-10-31 (child SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D): the gate index ended up
containing a single `tracked.txt` entry after `tests/test_test_cache.py`'s
`git()` helper ran `git add -A`, turning a green suite into an
unattributable verdict (three consecutive finish attempts).

## Fixed inline (child SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D)

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.git_env_for_repo(repo)` — new helper: scrubs
  repository overrides and keeps an ambient `GIT_INDEX_FILE` **only** when the
  index lives inside that repository's git directory.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — inspection commands (`git diff`,
  `git merge-base`, `compute_changed_files`) use it.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state`/`_run_git` use it, so a fixture
  repo's dirty-state fingerprint is no longer taken against a foreign index
  (which made every edit fingerprint identically and served stale cache hits).
- Hermetic `git()` helpers in `tests/test_test_cache.py`,
  `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`, `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py`,
  `skill/test/tests/test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py` (routed through
  `shared.git_sandbox.run_git`).

## Remaining scope (this item)

1. Sweep the remaining raw-git fixture helpers in `tests/` and
   `skill/*/tests/` (e.g. `test_implement_abort_safety.py`,
   `test_implement_code_freeze_gate.py`, `test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py`,
   `test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py`,
   `test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`) onto
   `shared.git_sandbox.run_git`.
2. Add a **guard** so this cannot regress: an autouse fixture (or a
   conftest-level assertion) that fails a test which changes the inherited
   index, with a clear remediation message — rather than the whole gate
   failing anonymously at the end of the suite.
3. Document the fixture rule in `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` next to the
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pass-through contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No test fixture stages into an inherited `GIT_INDEX_FILE`; the sweep is
      complete across `tests/` and `skill/*/tests/`.
- [ ] A guard fails the offending test (naming it) instead of the gate failing
      post-hoc with an unattributable verdict.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` documents the fixture rule and the guard.
- [ ] Proven by a fixture-level regression test plus a simulated gate run
      (index unchanged).

**Key Files:**
- skill/shared/git_sandbox.py
- skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py
- conftest.py
- docs/dev/test-isolation.md

## Goal

As an operator running dozens of concurrent agent sessions, I want a 1–3 second
changed-scope test run to start immediately instead of queueing 7–18 minutes behind
full suites on the host-wide `"test"` semaphore, and I want the runner to report slot
wait separately from execution time so a queue-delayed run can never again look like a
slow suite.

## Problem statement (measured 2026-10-31, llm repo, 44 concurrent sessions)

`_test_concurrency_slot()` acquires the shared `"test"` semaphore
(`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT = 2`, FIFO, no lane separation). With ~44 concurrent pi
sessions every test invocation — including partial runs whose pytest body takes
seconds — queues behind 7.3-minute full suites:

- `--scope changed`, pytest body `217 passed … in 1.83s` → call blocked **18.2 min**
- `--scope changed`, pytest body `297 passed … in 2.88s` → call blocked **14.3 min**
- `--scope changed`, pytest body `87 passed in 0.65s` → call blocked **7.5 min**

>99.7% of those wall clocks was semaphore wait. Aggregate cost: 447 `wait_for_job`
calls / 127 h of agent wall clock in one day, plus 458 `run_tests.py` calls / 11 h.

The ceiling is not a hardware limit: during saturation the host was 92% CPU idle
(load 3.7 / 32 threads, 53 GiB RAM free), two concurrent pytest processes each used
< 1 core, and full-suite duration is flat at 1-or-2 concurrency (382–465 s, n=41,
median 441 s). The pool ran at ~100% capacity in bursts (22 full suites in 83 min
= 161 min of work against 166 min of capacity), so queueing — not execution — is the
binding constraint.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Fast lane.** Partial runs (`--scope changed`, or `--type` other than `full`) acquire
   a separate host-wide semaphore namespace (`"test-fast"`, ceiling
   `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST`, default 4) that is independent of the `"test"` pool used
   by full suites, so a partial run never queues behind a running full suite. Full
   suites keep the `"test"` namespace. Cache hits still never acquire a slot.
2. **Re-derived full-suite ceiling.** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT` rises from 2 to 6,
   with the rationale (this work item id + `docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json` +
   the production measurement above) cited adjacent to the constant, matching the
   audit-knob precedent (SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE). Precedence (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` env >
   default), clamping (<1 → 1) and invalid-value warning are unchanged.
3. **Wait/execution split in the JSON.** Each suite result and the aggregate carry
   `slot_wait_seconds` alongside the existing timing; a slot-wait-only call is
   distinguishable from a slow suite without reading stderr.
4. **Lane is observable.** `--summary` (or the JSON `slot_lane` field) states which
   namespace and ceiling a run used, so an operator can tell why a run waited.
5. **Tests.** Deterministic unit tests cover: partial-run lane selection, full-suite lane
   selection, independent pools (a held full slot does not block a fast-lane acquire),
   `slot_wait_seconds` accounting, and the calibrated-default pinning test updated to the
   new value with both citations present.
6. **No regression.** The existing semaphore, nested-isolation, type/scope, and cache
   tests stay green; the runner's canonical command/cache keys are unchanged.

## Notes

- The earlier calibration slice (SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5, deleted) left a dormant pinning
  test in `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` keyed on
  `SA-0MVE995PV0077QB5` / `test-ceiling-validation.json`; this item supersedes it and
  re-points that test at the new evidence.
- Deliberate scope decision: no synthetic F7 fan-out this time. The production
  measurement is stronger evidence than a synthetic burst and needs no extra suite load
  on a host that is currently saturated by live sessions.

## Goal

As an operator whose machines are worktree-heavy, I want a long-lived branch
(`dev`/`main`) whose tracking config points at the repository itself to be
detected and repaired, so that a plain `git pull` can never silently fetch
nothing and leave that machine running stale agent infrastructure.

## Symptom (2026-10-31, rgardler-AI-Laptop)

```
$ git pull
From .
 * branch                dev        -> FETCH_HEAD
Already up to date.
$ git log --oneline -1
b50ccedc SA-0MVQHVKUH009VQMD: Implementation complete      # stale by 1+ commits
$ git config --get branch.dev.remote
.
```

`origin` was correct (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/SorraAgents.git`) and
`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev` showed the true tip, but plain `git pull`
uses `branch.dev.remote` — `.` — so it fetched **from the repository itself**
and reported success. That machine therefore kept running the pre-fix test
runner (2-slot pool) for hours after the fix landed on `dev`.

## Why it happens (verified in a scratch repo)

`branch.<name>.remote` is one key per **branch name**, shared by every worktree
through the common `.git/config`, and two supported operations write `.` into
it:

```
# worktree registration tracking a LOCAL base branch (implement.py:2339)
git worktree add --track -b wl-<id>-<slug> <path> dev
  -> branch.wl-<id>-<slug>.remote .   merge refs/heads/dev

# a push whose remote is the local path form
git push -u . dev:dev
  -> branch 'dev' set up to track './dev'.
     branch.dev.remote .             merge refs/heads/dev
```

`.` is the legitimate *worktree-ownership* signal for `wl-*` branches
(`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py:595-608`, `live_repo_guard.py:29`) and it
**survives `git worktree remove`**. On `dev`/`main` the same value is a trap:
`git pull` resolves to `refs/heads/dev` inside the same repository, prints
`From .` / `Already up to date`, and no remote data ever arrives. Nothing warns.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A guard (in `implement.py start`/`finish`, `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, or a
   `git for-each-ref`-based check) detects a **long-lived** branch whose
   `branch.<name>.remote` is `.` or whose `merge` resolves to itself, and emits
   an actionable warning naming the exact repair command.
2. The repair is one documented command
   (`git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/<branch> <branch>`) — verify it
   restores a working `git pull` from that machine.
3. The check is read-only and fail-open: it never rewrites tracking config on
   its own, and it never fires for `wl-*` worktree branches (where `.` is
   expected).
4. Deterministic tests cover: `remote=.` on `dev` detected; `remote=.` on a
   `wl-*` branch ignored; `remote=origin` clean; a self-referential `merge`
   (e.g. `merge=refs/heads/main` on `main`) detected.
5. Docs: one paragraph in the worktree-isolation / git-hooks docs explaining
   that `branch.<name>.remote` is shared per branch name and that `.` on a
   long-lived branch breaks `git pull` silently.

data.description:
# Intake Brief — long-lived branches whose upstream is `.` silently break `git pull`

**Priority: critical. Issue type: bug.**

## Summary

On a worktree-heavy machine, `dev` (or `main`) can end up with
`branch.<name>.remote = .`. Plain `git pull` then resolves the upstream to the
**same repository**, prints `From .` / `Already up to date`, exits 0, and no
remote data ever arrives. Every agent on that machine keeps running stale
skills/runner code while believing it is up to date, with no warning anywhere.

Observed live on 2026-10-31 (rgardler-AI-Laptop): the machine stayed on
`b50ccedc` for hours after `a2659c38` landed (the test-runner fix that removes
the 2-slot starvation), so it kept queueing every test run behind a 2-slot pool
while `origin` held the fixed runner. `origin` was configured correctly and
`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev` showed the true tip — only the
**branch-level** tracking key was wrong, and that is the key `git pull` reads.

## Evidence

```
$ git pull
From .
 * branch                dev        -> FETCH_HEAD
Already up to date.

$ git log --oneline -1
b50ccedc SA-0MVQHVKUH009VQMD: Implementation complete        # stale

$ git config --get branch.dev.remote
.
$ git config --get branch.dev.merge
refs/heads/dev

$ git remote -v
origin  git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/SorraAgents.git (fetch)   # correct
$ git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev
a2659c38f075d367668df5c3ffa48bcc8aeb75cb                     # true tip
```

Desktop counterpart, the healthy shape — long-lived branches point at `origin`,
only `wl-*` worktree branches use `.`:

```
[branch "main"]                                              remote = origin
[branch "dev"]                                               remote = origin
[branch "wl-SA-0MQSFWFB1007R2I7-extract-level-from-score"]   remote = .
[branch "wl-SA-0MSN6FBFS006Z5QP-implement-run-tests-canonical"] remote = .
...                                                          (all wl-* = .)
```

## Mechanism (reproduced in a scratch repo, not inferred)

`branch.<name>.remote` is **one key per branch name**, stored in the shared
`.git/config` that all worktrees use. Two supported operations write `.` into
it:

```bash
# 1. Worktree registration tracking a LOCAL base branch — implement.py:2339
git worktree add --track -b wl-<id>-<slug> <path> dev
  → branch.wl-<id>-<slug>.remote = .
    branch.wl-<id>-<slug>.merge  = refs/heads/dev

# 2. A push whose remote is the local path form
git push -u . dev:dev
  → branch 'dev' set up to track './dev'.
    branch.dev.remote = .
    branch.dev.merge  = refs/heads/dev

# (git branch --track dev dev / --set-upstream-to=dev dev refuse:
#  "not setting branch 'dev' as its own upstream", "--track needs a new branch")
```

For a `wl-*` branch `.` is the correct, intentional *worktree-ownership* signal
(`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py:595-608`, `live_repo_guard.py:29`) and it
**survives `git worktree remove`** — that survival is already load-bearing for
sandbox cleanup. On `dev`/`main` the identical value silently disables
`git pull` for the whole machine.

Why a fix, not just a guard: the write path is still live. As long as any tool
or operator can push with a path-form remote (`.`) or register a worktree on a
long-lived branch, a fresh clone can re-acquire the defect, and the failure mode
is silent success.

## Blast radius

- **Stale agent infrastructure.** Skills are symlinked into the checkout
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills -> <repo>/skill`), so a no-op pull means agents on that
  machine run old runner/gate/audit logic indefinitely. This already cost hours
  of queueing (the 2-slot `test` pool) after the fix had merged.
- **Stale worklog data.** `refs/worklog/data` is fetched on pull; a no-op pull
  means the machine's `wl` view diverges (stale statuses, missing items), and
  `wl sync` may then push a stale merge base.
- **Silent, so it compounds.** `git pull` exits 0, so scripts, agent sessions and
  the operator all conclude "up to date".
- Affects **both** repos on a machine (SorraAgents and llm-manager), plus any
  other worktree-managed checkout.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Detect.** A check reports every local branch whose tracking config resolves
   to itself — `branch.<name>.remote == "."` **or** `branch.<name>.merge`
   pointing at that same branch — and classifies it: **defect** for long-lived
   branches (`dev`, `main`, and any branch named in the repo's release config),
   **expected** for `wl-*` worktree branches, which must never be reported.
2. **Repair, machine-readable and safe.** One command (or `--fix`) repairs a
   defect to `remote=origin` / `merge=refs/heads/<branch>` **only** when
   `origin` is a real remote whose `refs/heads/<branch>` exists, otherwise it
   refuses with an actionable message (never guess a remote, never rewrite a
   `wl-*` branch, never touch `main`/`dev` working trees).
3. **Prevent — write path closed.** No framework code path can produce
   `remote=.` for a long-lived branch:
   - `implement.py` worktree creation keeps `--track` for the `wl-*` branch (the
     ownership signal is required) but asserts afterwards that the **parent**
     branch's tracking config is untouched, and fails loudly if a worktree
     registration ever writes `remote=.` onto the parent branch name;
   - any framework `git push` uses the configured remote **name** (`origin`),
     never a path/`.` form, so `-u` can never record a self-upstream;
   - a regression test proves both properties.
4. **Prevent — detection runs where it matters.** The check is wired into
   `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` (so the periodic/CI run reports it) and surfaced
   by `implement.py start` as a **warning** (fail-open: it must never block a
   work item, and must never rewrite config implicitly).
5. **Verification on a real machine.** After repair, `git pull` fetches from
   `origin` (not `.`), `git log origin/dev..dev` is empty, and the installed
   runner reports the current values (e.g.
   `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT=6`, `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST_DEFAULT=4`,
   `TEST_FAST_SEMAPHORE_NAME=test-fast`) — recorded as evidence on this item.
6. **Docs.** A short section in the worktree-isolation / git-hooks docs stating
   that `branch.<name>.remote` is shared per **branch name** across worktrees,
   that `.` is the legitimate worktree-ownership signal which survives
   `git worktree remove`, and that `.` on a long-lived branch makes `git pull`
   a silent no-op.
7. **Deterministic tests** (no network): scratch-repo fixtures for
   `worktree add --track -b X <path> dev` (X gets `.`, `dev` unchanged),
   `git push -u . dev:dev` (detected as a defect on `dev`), a self-referential
   `merge`, a healthy `origin`-tracked branch (no finding), and a `wl-*`
   branch with `.` (no finding).

## Out of scope

- Changing git's own semantics or rewriting `.` tracking for existing `wl-*`
  branches (required by sandbox cleanup).
- Auto-repairing machines without operator intent (the fix must be explicit;
  only detection is automatic).

## Affected machines / rollout

- `rgardler-AI-Laptop`: `dev` upstream is `.` in **both** SorraAgents and
  llm-manager — repair with
  `git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/dev dev`, then re-verify the runner and
  the stall-guard commit (`llm-manager` `dev` = `3b9c57f5`).
- Desktop (`sorra-agents-1`): verified healthy (`dev`/`main` = `origin`); no
  action.

## Supersedes

SA-0MVX1IIDL008RMMF (medium, detection-only guard) is folded into this item:
the guard is AC1/AC4 here, with the write-path prevention and repair added.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1** – implement.py finish leaves local dev behind after pushing to remote dev (completed)
- **SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66** – Stale local branch named origin/dev makes origin/dev ambiguous and breaks changed-scope test selection (open)
- **SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U** – Verified reversible local-dev sync + ancestry assertion (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac4, acceptance, acquire, action (+262 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0msn6fbfs006z5qp, ac1, ac4, acceptance, acquire (+245 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0msn6fbfs006z5qp, ac4, acquire, action, actionable (+241 more)

## Goal

Create deterministic, no-network scratch-repo test fixtures that verify the
self-referential upstream detection and repair logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`worktree add --track` does not corrupt parent.** A scratch repo with
   `dev` and `main` tracked at `origin` creates a `wl-*` worktree via
   `git worktree add --track -b wl-xxx <path> dev`. The test asserts:
   - `wl-*` branch has `remote = .` (expected)
   - `dev`/`main` remain at `remote = origin` (untouched)

2. **`git push -u . dev:dev` is detected as a defect.** A scratch repo with
   `dev` tracked at `origin` runs `git push -u . dev:dev`. The detection
   check reports `dev` as a **defect** (long-lived branch with `remote = .`).

3. **Self-referential `merge` is detected.** A scratch repo where
   `branch.dev.merge` points to `refs/heads/dev` (same branch) is reported
   as a defect even if `remote` is correct.

4. **Healthy `origin`-tracked branch is not flagged.** A scratch repo with
   `dev` and `main` tracked at `origin` produces **no findings**.

5. **`wl-*` branch with `.` is not flagged.** A scratch repo with a
   `wl-*` branch having `remote = .` produces **no findings** (expected
   for worktree branches).

## Deliverables

- Test script/fixtures in `skill/shared/tests/test_self_referential_upstream.py`
  (or equivalent shell-based test harness)
- Each fixture creates and destroys its own scratch repo (isolated)
- Exit 0 when all 5 tests pass; non-zero otherwise

config resolves to itself (`branch.<name>.remote == "."` or
`branch.<name>.merge` pointing at that same branch).

## Goal

Implement a safe `--fix` command that repairs a self-referential upstream
to `remote=origin` / `merge=refs/heads/<branch>`, only when the remote
exists and has the branch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Repairs defect to correct upstream.** A branch with
   `remote = .` / `merge = refs/heads/dev` is repaired to
   `remote = origin` / `merge = refs/heads/dev` when `origin` is a
   valid remote whose `refs/heads/dev` exists.

2. **Refuses when origin is missing or branch absent.** If `origin` remote
   does not exist, or `origin/refs/heads/<branch>` does not exist, the
   command refuses with an actionable error message (never guesses a
   remote, never rewrites to a non-existent branch).

3. **Never touches `wl-*` branches.** The repair command explicitly skips
   any branch matching `wl-*` (even if self-referential, as that is
   expected for worktree ownership).

4. **Never touches working trees.** The repair only modifies branch config
   (`.git/config`), never checks out or modifies working trees.

5. **Machine-readable confirmation.** After repair, outputs the before/after
   config in `--json` format.

## Deliverables

- Repair function integrated with the detection check (child 2)
- `--fix` flag that processes detected defects interactively or non-interactively
- Dry-run mode (`--dry-run`) for safety verification

# Test: FIFO fairness of test-slot acquisition

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC1, AC5). Test-first slice of the
starvation fix: pin arrival ordering **before** the turnstile lands, so the
implementing slice has an executable contract to satisfy.

## Why this must come first

The current `Semaphore.acquire()` polls the slot pool with a 50 ms jittered
retry; any later arrival can win a slot an older waiter has been polling for
hours (measured: one gate waited 2 h 9 min, `slot_busy` at 600/900/1800/2400/
7200 s bounds). Jitter (SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD) only staggers *deadlines* — it
never orders arrivals. A cross-process ordering test is what makes the fairness
property non-regressable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A cross-process unit test pins it: with one slot and four waiters started in a known order, slots are granted in arrival order and a later arrival never overtakes an earlier one (the fair, starvation-bounded slot acquisition contract of parent AC1).
- [ ] A test proves a waiter killed while queued or while holding a turn does not keep that turn — the next waiter acquires within a bounded time, preserving the kernel-`flock` crash-safety property (no stale locks, no PID bookkeeping).
- [ ] A test proves a fail-fast caller (`timeout=0`, as `audit_runner` uses) still acquires immediately when a slot is free even while tickets are outstanding, and still raises `TimeoutError` immediately when the pool is full (no turnstile deadlock).
- [ ] A test proves a nested run isolated through `nested_semaphore_dir` / `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` never queues in the host-wide turnstile while an outer run holds the host-wide slot.
- [ ] Ordering is asserted from recorded acquisition timestamps/sequence (not from sleep durations), holds are sub-second, and the whole test module stays well under the fast-lane budget.
- [ ] Tests use cross-process workers and the existing sandbox harness only — no ad-hoc suite invocations.

## Minimal implementation

1. Extend `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py`'s worker-template
   harness with an ordered-start variant (worker *i* starts only after worker
   *i-1* reports "arrived") and an acquisition-order log.
2. Add the killed-waiter test (SIGKILL a queued/holding worker; assert the next
   waiter acquires within a bound).
3. Add the fail-fast and nested-isolation tests to
   `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py`.
4. Mark the ordering tests to fail against today's implementation (red), then
   leave them for the implementing slice.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` — ordered-start worker harness and arrival-order assertions
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — fail-fast caller and nested-namespace compatibility tests
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — the module under test (read-only for this slice)

## Constraints

- No production code changes in this slice (tests only, expected red until the implementing slice lands).
- No ad-hoc test-suite invocations: run through `/skill:test` (or the changed-scope gate inside `implement.py finish`).
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- Ordering, crash-reclaim, fail-fast and nested-isolation tests, committed and red-then-green with the implementing slice.

## Dependencies

- None. Blocks the turnstile implementation slice.

# Test: gate_reason classification for pre-push and finish

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC2, AC3, AC5). Test-first slice of the
dev-push reporting work: the classifier contract, the hook output and the
finish-side report are pinned before any of them is implemented.

## Why this must come first

`.githooks/pre-push` currently runs the runner with `--json >/dev/null 2>&1`
and prints the same "ERROR: Full test suite failed" for a red suite, an
expired slot wait and a killed run — the JSON that already carries
`notice_codes` is discarded. `implement.py finish` then reports
`reason: push_failed` with no cause. The classification contract has to be
executable before either side is changed.

- [ ] Unit tests pin the classifier: every runner `notice_code` (`slot_busy`, `suite_timeout`, `killed`, `unparsed_failure`, `command_not_found`), a structured `failures` list, a `live_repo_mutation` notice, and an unparsable/absent JSON result each map to the documented `gate_reason` code.

# Test: push transport-retry policy

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC4, AC5). Test-first slice of the
transport-retry work.

## Why this must come first

Three pushes needed a manual retry loop after a green cached gate followed by
`Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` — `git_push_to_dev()`
currently returns `False` on any non-timeout, non-non-fast-forward failure, so
the caller cannot tell "retry later" from "fix the code". The retry policy
(retryable patterns, attempt bound, backoff, same cwd, no gate bypass) must be
pinned before it is implemented so the allowlist can never silently widen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test pins the retryable patterns: `Connection to … closed by remote host`, `Connection reset by peer`, `remote end hung up unexpectedly` and `kex_exchange_identification` are retried; auth, branch-policy and other errors are not.
- [ ] A test pins the attempt bound (initial attempt plus two retries) and jittered exponential backoff, and asserts a `PushTimeoutError` is never retried.
- [ ] A test asserts every attempt uses the **same cwd** as the first attempt and the same argv/env — no `--no-verify`, no `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` or other bypass injection — so the pre-push gate runs again and serves its cached full-suite entry.
- [ ] A test asserts non-fast-forward failures keep their existing dedicated recovery (no transport retry) and that an exhausted retry trail reports the attempt count, the backoff used and the final reason.
- [ ] Stubs only (a fake `Popen`/process factory plus the hermetic git sandbox); no ad-hoc suite invocations and no real network access.
- [ ] Across the three test slices, new/updated tests cover FIFO fairness (cross-process), hook classification of slot-busy vs red suite vs timeout, finish reporting of a gate infrastructure failure, and transport-retry policy (retryable vs non-retryable stderr, attempt bound, same cwd) — tests use stubs/hermetic git sandboxes only, with no ad-hoc suite invocations.

## Minimal implementation

1. New module `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` with a
   recording fake process factory driven by a scripted stderr/return-code
   sequence, and a `time.sleep` spy for the backoff.
2. Table-driven cases for retryable vs non-retryable stderr.
3. Same-cwd / same-argv / same-env assertions across attempts.
4. Leave the tests red for the implementing slice.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — new: retry policy, attempt bound, same-cwd, no-bypass assertions
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` under test
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — existing push-timeout contract to stay consistent with

## Constraints

- Tests only; no production code in this slice.
- No network access and no real long sleeps (monkeypatch the sleep).
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- Retry-policy test module, red then green with the implementing slice.

## Dependencies

- None. Blocks the transport-retry implementation slice.
