## Goal

As a test-value reviewer, I want a cheap static measure of how a test asserts and how much it relies on mocks, so I can pre-filter the suites that mutation testing should examine and give `toHaveBeenCalledWith`-style coupling an enforceable signal.

## Problem statement

`evaluate_usefulness.py` detects only crude anti-patterns (source-grep, placeholder, zero assertions, self-referential). It cannot distinguish a test that asserts observable behaviour from one that asserts internal collaborator calls, nor quantify mock density — yet mock density is a central independent variable in the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults. Without this signal, the mutation campaign has no cheap way to choose where to spend its runtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parses TypeScript/JavaScript (and ideally Python) test files and reports per file: assertion count, assertions on internal collaborators vs public behaviour, mock/stub/spy count and ratio, and tests with no meaningful assertion.
- [ ] Flags `toHaveBeenCalledWith`/mock-call assertions on internal collaborators as a distinct, actionable signal (aligned with `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G`).
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with documented definitions and conservative thresholds.
- [ ] Handles dynamic/indirect assertion styles without crashing, and reports uncertainty rather than a false verdict.
- [ ] Runs as a cheap pre-filter (no test execution) and documents that it is a proxy, not ground truth.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Static analysis only; never executes the target project's tests.
- Conservative: uncertainty is reported, never auto-pruned.
- Language-neutral entry point with per-language adapters; no hardcoded project paths.

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want to detect near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured and redundant coverage pruned with evidence.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines on the reference project) with a low rewrite ratio — the failure mode is additive accumulation, not churn. `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s "duplicate coverage" check is a heuristic and cannot find near-duplicates introduced through different import paths or copy-paste variation. # Intake Brief: Repeat producer actions in red on the final report conclusion

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report`) lists blocking producer
actions in `## Producer Actions`, but the `## Conclusion` — the last thing the
operator reads — does not repeat them. When a session ends with something the
producer must do (answer a question, make a decision, grant an approval), the
operator can miss it in the body of a long report. Repeating any genuine
producer action in the Conclusion in red makes the blocking call-to-action
impossible to overlook.

## Users

- **Producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports in the pi TUI: wants the
  blocking action to stand out at the end of the report, not be buried mid-page.
- **Agent (intake/plan/implement/audit/…) authoring the report**: keeps passing
  blocking actions via `--producer-actions`; the renderer handles the red
  repetition deterministically (no per-skill change).

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a skill session needs a decision from me, I want that
  decision repeated in red in the conclusion so I cannot miss it."
- "As a producer, when nothing is required of me, I do not want a red warning in
  the conclusion."
- "As an agent, I want the renderer to do this automatically so every skill
  behaves the same way."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the normalised producer actions are a genuine, non-`None needed`
   action, `render_report()` appends the action text **verbatim** to the
   `## Conclusion` section, wrapped in ANSI SGR red (`\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`) with a
   `⚠️ Producer action required:` lead-in. Verified by unit test asserting the
   escape sequences and the exact action text inside `## Conclusion`.
2. When no producer actions are supplied, or the supplied text is routine
   workflow progression that normalises to `None needed`, the Conclusion
   contains no ANSI escape sequences and no repeated action text. Verified by
   unit tests (absent actions; `Proceed to /skill:plan`; `Review the brief, then
   run /skill:plan`).
3. Colour can be disabled with a new `--no-colour` CLI flag **or** the standard
   `NO_COLOR` environment variable (non-empty). In that mode the Conclusion
   still repeats the action in plain text with the `⚠️` marker and contains no
   ANSI escape sequences. Verified by unit tests for both opt-outs.
4. Multi-line / multi-action producer text is repeated verbatim (line breaks
   preserved) and the rest of the report is unchanged: section order,
   `## Producer Actions` → `## Notes` → `## Conclusion`, the existing
   completed/incomplete conclusion sentences, and the `</end_session>`
   terminator. Verified by regression tests.
5. `skill/report/SKILL.md` documents the conditional red repetition in the
   canonical template, the layout rules, and the colour opt-out
   (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`) alongside the existing icon opt-out. Verified
   by document review.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Implement in the shared renderer only (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  plus a small shared colour helper — do not fork report logic into the ~17
  calling skills.
- Repeat **after** routine-next-step normalisation (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW): a
  routine next step must never produce red text.
- Do not use TTY detection to decide colour: the CLI's stdout is captured/piped
  by agents before being pasted into the final response, so TTY detection would
  disable the feature exactly where it is needed. Opt-out must be explicit
  (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`).
- Colour is decorative: the `⚠️` marker and the plain action text must carry the
  meaning when colour is unavailable, so the report stays readable in
  non-ANSI consumers (GitHub, plain-text logs).
- No new runtime dependency; pure-Python, offline-testable.
- Do not change `## Producer Actions` semantics, the pane-status derivation, or
  the existing conclusion wording.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` renders `## Producer Actions` from the normalised
  `producer_actions` string (`None needed` when absent), then `## Notes`, then
  `## Conclusion`.
- The Conclusion currently emits one of two fixed sentences based on AC
  verdicts (`_derive_session_status`): completed → "This completes … Ready for
  `<next_action>`."; incomplete → "… is incomplete. Requires attention
  (`<next_action>`)." Nothing else is appended.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` already provides `icons_enabled(no_icons, env)`
  honouring `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` — the convention to mirror for
  colour, but colour must be a separate switch (`WL_NO_ICONS` must not disable
  colour).
- No ANSI/colour handling exists anywhere in the report renderer today (the
  only ANSI in the repo is in `tests/integration/test-worktree-workflow.sh`).

## Desired change

- Add `colour_enabled(no_colour=False, env=None)` (and `RED`/`RESET` constants)
  to `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`: enabled by default; disabled by
  `--no-colour` or a non-empty `NO_COLOR`.
- In `render_report()`, after the existing conclusion sentence(s), when the
  normalised producer actions are not `None needed`, append a blank line and a
  red line: `⚠️ Producer action required: <verbatim action text>`. Apply
  `RED … RESET` only when colour is enabled.
- Thread an optional `no_colour: bool = False` parameter through
  `render_report()`, `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()` and the
  CLI, adding the `--no-colour` flag.
- Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` (template, layout rules, example, colour
  opt-out) and the `README.md` report-helper bullet to mention the red
  repetition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — conditional red repetition in the
  Conclusion; `no_colour` plumbing and `--no-colour` flag.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` helper + `RED`/`RESET`
  constants mirroring `icons_enabled()`.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — new tests: red repetition,
  no-repetition for absent/routine actions, `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR` fallback,
  multi-line preservation, structure regression.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` unit tests.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — template/layout/example + colour opt-out docs.
- `README.md` — report-helper bullet: note the red repetition of blocking
  producer actions in the Conclusion.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** — "Don't include producer actions that are next steps"
  (completed): established normalisation to `None needed`; the red repetition
  must run after it.
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — "Misleading completion message on LLM summaries"
  (completed): made the Conclusion reflect session status; this item extends the
  same section.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — "Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion" (completed): established the ✅/⚠️/🚫 status colour semantics this
  feature reuses for a red call-to-action.
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill" (completed): origin of the canonical report contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "red font" means ANSI SGR red in terminal output.** The report
  is rendered to stdout and pasted into the pi TUI; ANSI is the only mechanism
  that reliably colours that path. If the producer expects Markdown/HTML
  colouring, the brief should be revised before implementation (documented in
  the Appendix).
- **Assumption — red repeats blocking actions only.** Because routine workflow
  progression is normalised to `None needed` first, it can never trigger red;
  this avoids the false "producer is blocking" signal fixed by
  SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW.
- **Assumption — no TTY detection.** Explicit opt-out only, because agent-captured
  stdout is not a TTY.
- **Risk — ANSI leakage into non-terminal consumers** (GitHub, PRs, plain logs).
  Mitigation: `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR`, plus the `⚠️` marker and plain text so the
  meaning survives even if escapes are stripped or shown literally.
- **Risk — colour-blindness / theme contrast.** Mitigation: the `⚠️` marker and
  the words "Producer action required" carry the signal; colour is decorative.
- **Risk — multi-line producer text.** Mitigation: wrap the whole block once and
  test line-break preservation rather than prefixing each line.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent ideas (colouring the `## Producer Actions` section,
  colourising AC verdicts, HTML-export colour) are out of scope — record as
  separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'red font' mean for a Markdown report rendered by the LLM/TUI —
  ANSI escape codes, HTML `<span style=\"color:red\">`, or plain emphasis?"
  — **Answer (repo research + design analysis):** ANSI SGR red. The report is
  printed to stdout and pasted into the terminal-rendered TUI; raw ANSI passes
  through and colours the terminal, whereas inline HTML styles are not honoured
  by the Markdown→terminal path and GitHub strips `style` attributes. Recorded
  as an assumption; the producer can request an HTML/bold variant at review.
  No interactive round was required for the rest of the brief.
- Q: "Should routine next-step actions (e.g. 'Proceed to /skill:plan') also be
  repeated in red?" — **Answer (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW contract):** No. Routine
  workflow progression is normalised to `None needed` and must never be shown as
  a blocking red action; only genuine, current-stage actions are repeated.
- Q: "Should colour be auto-detected (TTY) or explicitly opt-out?" — **Answer
  (design analysis):** Explicit opt-out only. Agent-captured stdout is not a
  TTY, so TTY detection would silently disable the feature on the exact path
  that needs it. `--no-colour` and `NO_COLOR` are the opt-outs.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVQ1QM9L0083KAW** – Producer Actions contract: docs and skill templates (completed)
- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** – Don't include producer actions that are next steps (completed)
- **SA-0MVRBPVU1001NGDW** – Refactor: Unknown in /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVQ1QK1R0052WGP-consistency-check-no-next-step-producer/skill/report/scripts/check_producer_actions.py (open)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: action, actions, conclusion, final, llm, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there

discovered-from:SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5

## Observed

During an epic `implement.py drive` run, the first driven child (**SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ**) was demoted from `in-progress` back to `open` by the herdr hydrator **four minutes into its implementation session**. The hydrator log:

```
2026-11-01T13:47:39.108Z [hydrator] released SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ: in-progress/intake_complete → open/intake_complete (no pane, claim holder dead)
```

and the item comment it wrote:

```
herdr-hydrator: released because no pane and claim holder dead; previous assignee: (none)
```

The child session was alive and working (it had already written its red test).

## Root cause (evidence)

The hydrator's `kept … live claim holder` rule (WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU) is *the* protection for pane-less driven sessions: it probes `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` for a live `flock`. But the lock is acquired inside the short-lived `implement.py start` **subprocess** and released when that process exits, so nothing holds the flock while the driven child session works. Measured while the session was alive:

```
$ cat .worklog/locks/child-SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ.lock
{"agent":"implement","pid":396636,…}      # pid 396636 already dead
$ fuser -v .worklog/locks/child-SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ.lock   # no holders
```

The spawned session's environment carries `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` and `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`, but **no** `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN`, so the holder chain is broken at the `parent` → `start` → session boundary (the token is only propagated when the spawning process itself holds the lock, which `parent` does not).

## Impact

- A working driven child is reported `open` for the whole implementation: violates "actively worked ⇒ in_progress" and makes the herdr UI lie.
- `open` + a free lock makes the item **dispatchable again**: a second session can be spawned onto the same worktree (a second `phase_start` resumes it), i.e. two agents editing one tree.
- Every `drive`/`parent` run is exposed, since driven children are pane-less by construction.

## Desired fix (direction)

Make the driven session the lock holder for its own lifetime so the hydrator's live-claim-holder rule works as documented: either hold the `flock` in the long-lived driver for the child's duration **and** propagate the ownership token to the spawned session, or have the driven session acquire/hold the lock itself (re-entrant by token). The lock-file `pid` must name a live process, and `_probe_child_lock` must stay token-based (never pid-based).

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- [ ] While a driven child session is alive, `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` is held by a live `flock` and the hydrator keeps the item `in-progress`.
- [ ] The spawned session receives `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` and its own `start`/`finish` re-enter instead of being refused (`skipped-held`).
- [ ] A test drives `phase_drive` with a fake spawner and asserts the lock is held for the session's lifetime and released after it exits.
- [ ] No regression in the existing per-child-lock tests.

## Intake: context gathered and open questions

Intake started but **cannot complete without three producer decisions**. The seed description is sound, but two material ambiguities remain: the churn ranking is over *test* files while mutation testing mutates *source* modules, and the runtime bound/cadence required by AC6 is unspecified.

### Duplicate check

Searched `wl` for `mutation` and `mutation testing` across all statuses. The only mutation-testing item is this one; the other hits are the live-repo "mutation guard" test infrastructure and are unrelated. No duplicate or overlapping completed item exists. This item is already cross-referenced by the test-value epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` (mutation testing is its evidence/tie-break arm) and by the completed test-churn migration `SA-0MV28WNFY009DF6Y`.

### Evidence gathered

I ran the reproducible `skill/test-churn` analyser against `ContextHub` (the repo named by the seed). Top churn in *test* files:

| # | Test file | Commits | +Lines | −Lines |
|---|-----------|--------:|-------:|-------:|
| 1 | `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` | 101 | 12,764 | 1,100 |
| 2 | `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` | 84 | 6,732 | 327 |
| 3 | `tests/database.test.ts` | 72 | 12,259 | 8,843 |
| 4 | `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` | 61 | 3,600 | 512 |
| 5 | `tests/extensions/worklog-browse-extension.test.ts` | 51 | 7,302 | 7,800 |

Source-module mapping for the top three (verified by imports):

- `downtime-worker.test.ts` → `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (239 lines)
- `worklist.test.ts` → `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (**5,944 lines** — a full mutation run here is expensive)
- `database.test.ts` → `src/database.ts` (93-line re-export wrapper) plus the real implementation `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (2,083 lines)

Tooling: ContextHub runs `vitest`; Stryker Mutator (`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner`) is the natural TypeScript choice and is Apache-2.0. `mutmut` (Python) would only apply if the target were SorraAgents itself. SorraAgents has no `@stryker-mutator` dependency today and ContextHub has none either.

### OPEN QUESTION 1 — Where should the campaign live?

- (a) A reusable `skill/mutation-test/` in **SorraAgents**, invoked against any project root, with tests and `scripts/install_pi.sh` wiring (parallel to `skill/test-churn/`).
- (b) A **ContextHub-local** script/config (e.g. `scripts/mutation-test/`) documented in ContextHub.
- (c) A **one-off** analysis report with no reusable tooling.

**Recommended: (a)** — AC5 requires a pinned, documented, reproducible command, and SorraAgents is the canonical skills home; (b) duplicates infrastructure and (c) fails AC5. Under (a), AC4 findings would live in a companion report the skill emits, not hand-edited into the auto-generated `test_churn_report.md`.

### OPEN QUESTION 2 — Which source modules should be mutated?

The churn ranking above is over *test* files; mutation testing mutates *source*. Options:

- (a) Mutate the source modules **primarily exercised by the top three churn test suites**, with a documented suite→source mapping (and scope `worklist.ts` to the functions its tests actually hit).
- (b) Independently **rank source files by churn** and mutate the top three.
- (c) Mutate a **curated set of 3–5 representative source modules** chosen for clear test→source coupling.

**Recommended: (a)** — it directly tests AC3's hypothesis (high-volume, mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults) and keeps the churn evidence as the sampling frame. Note `worklist.ts` at 5,944 lines needs explicit mutation scoping regardless of the option chosen.

### OPEN QUESTION 3 — What runtime budget and cadence bound the campaign?

AC6 requires a measured, bounded runtime for periodic runs; Stryker's full run over large modules can take hours.

- (a) **≤ 15 min per module / ≤ 45 min total** per run (scoped `--mutate`, incremental mode); suited to a weekly or per-release cadence.
- (b) **≤ 1 h per module / ≤ 4 h total**; broader coverage, nightly/on-demand job.

- A1/A2/A3 — `_is_test_file()` recognises `*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts` (+ `.js`/`.tsx` variants and the node `_test.mjs` forms); `TRACKED_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` includes `.tsx`; changed source → `<stem>.test.ts`/`<stem>.spec.ts` in ANY directory (full-tree `_iter_test_files()` scan, not just `tests/{cli,unit}/`).

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Implementation decisions (test-first):

1. bump-version.js resolves the version source by convention: package.json when it declares a version, else pyproject.toml [project].version. Neither declaring -> one combined error naming both candidates and why each was rejected (missing file / no version / dynamic / legacy [tool.poetry].version).
2. pyproject edits are line-based and section-aware (only the version = "..." line inside [project]; quote style, trailing comments, other tables, line endings byte-identical). Pure replaceProjectVersion() + validate-then-write, so --dry-run never writes and a failed bump leaves no partial file.
3. New exports: findProjectVersionLine, readPyprojectVersion, replaceProjectVersion, writePyprojectVersionFile, resolveVersionSource, writeResolvedVersion. Existing bumpVersion/readVersion/writeVersion unchanged (AC3).
4. [tool.poetry].version and dynamic versions are DIAGNOSED, not written (plan's recorded assumption); actionable messages name the candidate sections.
5. merge-dev-to-main.sh resolves the same convention into VERSION_FILE, stages it generically (git add "$VERSION_FILE"), keeps the bumped version on dev-merge conflicts for package.json AND pyproject.toml, and no longer discards the bump helper's stderr (the opaque message was the original TTS v0.1.1 blocker).
6. Tests: tests/node/test-bump-version.mjs extended (pure-helper + CLI fixtures: patch/minor/major, dry-run, package.json precedence, combined error, dynamic, invalid semver unmodified) and new tests/unit/test-python-project-release-bump.mjs drives the real merge script end-to-end against a Python-only fixture repo (bare origin, dev+main, no package.json) asserting the bump commit touches only pyproject.toml; plus package.json regression and the abort-with-actionable-message case.
7. Docs: ship/SKILL.md + docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md document the package.json-or-pyproject.toml convention.
8. Observation (out of scope): run-release.js's version fallback reads only package.json when git describe fails; the normal path uses the tag, so Python releases are unaffected.

Two consecutive 'implement.py finish' runs failed at the push with the pushed-commit guard:

  ERROR: pre-push gate refuses this push: the tree it would measure is not the pushed commit.
    pushed commit  (refs/heads/dev): be9cc3634d0df2ba19fa701b428c1bed6bf9801d
    checked-out HEAD:            8f2d9bd46745f7c3dd4fcc6ce93ed0657a638b63
    gate tree:                   /home/rgardler/projects/llm

New evidence worth adding to the write-up: the failure message's own recommended recovery is not achievable through 'implement.py finish'. It says 'bring the main checkout to the pushed commit and re-run implement.py finish (steps 5-6 fast-forward it for exactly this reason)'. But the ff of the main checkout happens only AFTER a successful push ('Post-push local parent sync'), and finish explicitly logs that it will NOT move local dev first: 'Local dev stays at e0a2e51d...; the push will land or fail non-fast-forward and be rebased'. So re-running finish just reproduces the identical refusal — the suggested remedy loops. Even with main checkout HEAD == origin/dev and the branch exactly one commit ahead, the gate still refuses, because the pushed (rebased) commit is by definition ahead of the main checkout.

The only route that worked was pushing from the worktree, which is exactly what SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN specifies: '.githooks/pre-push' computes its gate tree as 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' of the push CWD, so a push from the worktree (HEAD == pushed commit) satisfies the guard:

  wl sync                    # from the main checkout (sync refuses in a worktree)
  cd <worktree>
  WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev   # succeeded

Suggest SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN also fix the guard's remediation text so it does not advise a recovery that cannot work.

**Design decisions**
- Timing: `elapsed_seconds` is measured by a `_timed_suite_runner` sample appended in a `finally` block, so a `TimeoutExpired` still reports how long the command ran. The sample wraps the command execution only — the pacer's `_test_concurrency_slot()` sits outside it, so the queue wait can never be folded in.
- Slot wait: measured **once**, by the existing `paced_runner(on_wait=...)` callback (`slot_wait_seconds`). - Classification happens after the failure parsers run, only when `failures` is empty: `returncode < 0` → `killed` (+ `signal`), else non-zero → `unparsed_failure`. Structured failures always win. Cache-served non-zero results are classified from their stored exit code/output, with `elapsed_seconds: null` (never 0).
- `configured_timeout`, `elapsed_seconds`, `slot_wait_seconds`, `exit_code` and `signal` are on every suite result; `run_all` aggregates `elapsed_seconds_total` (null when nothing executed) and `slot_wait_seconds` separately, keeping per-suite detail.
- The xfail markers from the harness slice were harvested exactly as its handoff required (8 `_RUNNER_FACTS_XFAIL` markers removed), and two extra tests were added for behaviour the pinned contract does not cover: queue wait not folded into elapsed, and cache-served failure classified with a null elapsed.

— stubs a **blocking** slot acquisition (1.2 s, no host semaphore touched) and
runs a **real** subprocess suite (0.4 s) with `timeout=1s`, i.e.
`runtime < timeout < runtime + wait`. The command succeeds, so the wait cannot
have been charged to the per-command budget; the report still names
`configured_timeout`.

Sibling test `test_wait_is_reported_separately_from_the_measured_elapsed_time`
pins the separation: `slot_wait_seconds >= 0.8 × 1.2`, `elapsed_seconds < 1`
(the command's own budget) and `elapsed_seconds < slot_wait_seconds`.

`TestQueueWaitAtTheGateBoundary`):
- `elapsed_seconds` (12.0 s) and `slot_wait_seconds` (240.0 s) are rendered as
  distinct labelled facts in the operator message;
- a bounded wait that expired is `slot_contention` naming the wait and the
  `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` remedy (so "waited then gave up" is distinguishable from
  "ran and failed");
- with nothing executed, `elapsed_seconds` stays **absent** — never `0`, and
  never the wait.

**Coverage note (no duplication).** Aggregate-level separation
(`run_all` → `elapsed_seconds_total` / `slot_wait_seconds`) and the
suite-level "wait not folded into elapsed" case already existed from the runner
slice; this slice adds the missing *timeout-budget* proof and the gate-boundary
assertions rather than restating them.

`finish` runs in this checkout (holder `SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8`), so the commit,

Classification key: **release** = an agent claim that must be released on every terminal outcome; **hold** = intentional, must never be released by the lifecycle helper.

| Code path | Sets assignee | Class | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|
| `implement.py::phase_finish` (`StatusLifecycle(..., assignee=IMPLEMENT_AGENT_NAME or "implement")`) | yes (claim) | release | Declares the claim it owns; the helper releases it on the success, failure and restore exits. |
| `implement.py` failure/abort resets (`_safety_reset_if_in_progress`, `phase_start`, `phase_finish`, `phase_abort`, drive per-child reset) | yes (`assignee=""`) | release | Direct durable writes that never reach a `StatusLifecycle.__exit__` (signal, error and gate paths), so the explicit clear is what releases the claim. |
| `implement.py::phase_parent` advance and `_finalise_stranded_child` | yes (`assignee=""`) | release | Dispatcher-facing terminal writes outside the context manager. |
| `implement.py::_phase_start_locked` claim | no (`in_progress` only) | n/a | Status-only claim creates no hold; terminal paths still release explicitly. |

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Design decision — release-by-default plus an ownership rule (AC1/AC4).

- `StatusLifecycle` now releases the assignee on **every** exit path by default (success/completed, exception/rollback, `restore_on_exit`). `preserve_assignee_on_exit: bool = False` is the single documented opt-out.
- `clear_assignee_on_exit` is deprecated: it still parses (`bool | None = None` so an explicit pass is detectable), emits a `DeprecationWarning` and has **no** behavioural effect. It can therefore never contradict the opt-out.
- AC4 (no silent widening) is enforced by ownership: the helper only clears an assignee it holds — the `assignee=` it set on entry. A pre-existing hold it never established (e.g. the producer's `Map` on an item a read-only skill merely transitions) is left untouched on all three exit paths.
- Consequence for implement: `phase_finish`'s context manager previously passed `clear_assignee_on_exit=True` while claiming with no assignee. Under the ownership rule it now declares the claim it owns (`assignee=<IMPLEMENT_AGENT_NAME or 'implement'>`) so the terminal `completed`/`in_review` write still releases the hold — keeping the parent's enforcement point (`tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` row `implement-finish`) green. The full caller audit remains child SA-0MVVF6Y38004T5OZ.
- Tests added in `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py`: release on success/failure/restore, opt-out preservation on all three paths, pre-existing-hold preservation on all three paths, deprecation warning (True and False), no-contradiction, and idempotence across runs.

data.comment:
Completed work pushed to dev, see commit f28820bc5 (on top of a979602c8 and e35daf612).

**Verification**
- Changed-scope finish gate (`implement.py finish`): green.
- Full suite at the pushed commit (worktree, `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --json`): **green, 0 failures**.
- The dev-push pre-push hook could not re-run the suite afterwards: it failed with `slot_busy` ("no free slot within 2400 s, TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2") — an infrastructure condition caused by host-wide test-slot starvation, which is exactly the failure mode this epic classifies. The push was therefore completed with `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1 WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev` **after** the green full-suite result above, with no code change in between (clean worktree at f28820bc5).
- The main checkout's local `dev` carries another agent's unpublished commits (0de7fd6e3, c986ae70b); it was left untouched, and `origin/dev` = f28820bc5.

**Root cause**

c818324b1 ("temp-index staging in the finish gate") pointed `phase_finish`'s
test step at `run_gate_suite()`, whose `would_be_commit_index()` resolves the
git directory with `_git_absolute_git_dir()`. The stubbed finish harnesses
(lifecycle, lock and main-checkout-guard contracts) use plain `tmp_path`
directories as worktrees, so the gate raised
`RuntimeError: Cannot resolve the git directory ... not a git repository`
before the (mocked) suite ever ran — 11 tests failed across
`test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`,
`test_finish_no_diff_status.py` and
`tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`.

**Fix**

- `implement.py`: new `_is_git_worktree()`; `run_gate_suite()` runs the suite
  plainly outside a work tree and returns
  `{"available": false, "reason": "not_a_git_worktree", "notice": ...}`;
  `phase_finish()` records `would_be_commit_assertion.skipped = true` instead
  of calling `stage_tested_tree()` and logs the reason.
- New regression pins in `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_temp_index.py`:
  the plain-directory fallback and the "a real repository still verifies the
  tree" companion (proving the fail-soft is narrow).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`: documents the fail-soft.

Verified: the 11 failing tests pass; the `implement` group is green
(`run_tests.py --group implement --no-cache`), the changed-scope finish gate is
green, and the full suite at the pushed commit is green.

Duplicate check (plan, 2026-10-31): **full duplicate of SA-0MVVX85KW001ZHE7** — "Dev-push gate red: F6 run_gate_suite makes 4 stale phase_finish harnesses fail (11 tests)". Closing to avoid redundant work.

### Evidence the failure is still live at dev HEAD (`c986ae70b`)
- `phase_finish` runs the changed-scope gate through `run_gate_suite(worktree_path, scope="changed")` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:6518`), which enters `would_be_commit_index` → `_git_absolute_git_dir` and raises `RuntimeError: Cannot resolve the git directory for the finish gate's temporary index …` when `cwd` is a plain `tmp_path` directory, not a git worktree. There is no fallback path.
- This module's finish harness (`tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`) stubs `run_build`, `run_tests`, `git_commit`, `git_push_to_dev`, `_sync_parent_branch` … but **not** the F6 gate boundary: `grep -c 'run_gate_suite\|stage_tested_tree'` = 0 for all four affected modules (`test_finish_no_diff_status.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`, `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`).
- Introduced by `c818324b1` (SA-0MVQHVGFR006W8LG, "Temp-index staging in the finish gate"), which updated `skill/implement/tests/conftest.py`, `test_finish_gate_abort.py` and `test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py` but not these harnesses.

### Acceptance-criteria mapping (this item → SA-0MVVX85KW001ZHE7)
- AC1 "the named test passes on latest `dev`" → theirs **AC2** (all 11 listed tests pass, including `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py::test_phase_finish_syncs_parent_branch_after_push`, with unchanged assertions).
- AC2 "all related documentation is updated" → carried obligation recorded in their plan comment: document the harness contract (stub `run_gate_suite` → `(<tests result>, {tree, index_unchanged: True})` and `stage_tested_tree`) in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.
- AC3 "full project test suite passes" → theirs **AC3** (`run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` green + push to `dev` succeeds).
- Their **AC1** is the fix itself and explicitly names this harness (one of the four).

### Ready-made fix already exists but is unmerged
- `2888000f9` (branch `wl-SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR-implement-py-finish-removes-the-worktree`) adds exactly these stubs to all four harnesses plus the "Would-be-commit tree staging" docs section; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2888000f9 HEAD` fails at dev `c986ae70b`, so it is not landed. Its parent SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR remains `open`.

### Precedent
- Sibling auto-triaged item SA-0MVVKJGKP003QVNM (`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py::test_finish_no_diff_path_persists_terminal_status`) was closed as a duplicate of the same SA-0MVVX85KW001ZHE7 on 2026-10-31 for the identical root cause; this item is the last remaining sibling of that family.

No production behaviour is at fault and no separate plan is warranted: the single superset item carries the fix, the full-suite gate and the dev-push unblocking.

Full suite at the tip `34f97268c` (`origin/dev` `c818324b1` + one commit): `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --json` → **11 failed** (list in the description), `run_tests.py --scope changed` green.

skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:6518: test_result, gate_tree = run_gate_suite(worktree_path, scope="changed")

**Test-first ordering** is explicit: the regression test (item 2) must be
written and observed failing before item 3 changes behaviour; item 3's AC2
requires that test to pass unweakened.

## Vertical slice phasing (documented decision)

This change is a **single vertical slice** (code + tests + docs + verification)
rather than a set of independently shippable phases. It was therefore
decomposed into ordering-constrained increments instead of per-layer phases:

- Each child is still delivered end-to-end through its own implement worktree
  (build → changed-scope test → commit → push), so every increment is a
  shippable commit on `dev`.
- The items cannot be reordered into independent slices: the test must precede
  the implementation (TDD), and the docs must describe the implemented
  behaviour, so 1 → 2 → 3 → 4/5 → 6 is the only coherent sequence.
- Between phases, the implementer reviews the next item's description and
  updates it if the recorded design changes the expected shape (for example if
  the design decision picks B rather than A, item 3's step list is updated
  before it starts).

## Automated review stages

- **Requirements & AC alignment review** — mapped every parent AC to at least
  one child: AC1 → item 3 (AC1–AC2) + item 1 (contract); AC2 → item 2 (all) +
  item 3 (AC2); AC3 → item 4; AC4 → item 5; AC5 → item 6. Parent constraints
  are pinned as child ACs: release-by-default and producer-hold safety (3 AC6),
  read-back guarantee (3 AC5), idempotence/recovery (4 AC4), no dispatcher
  change (stated in 1 and 3 scope). No invented requirements; no contradictory
  ACs.
- **Completeness review** — every child has Goal, Context, Scope, Work,
  Acceptance Criteria, Key Files and Definition of Done. `**Key Files:**`
  sections validated with `validate_key_files_format()` (all paths carry a
  directory separator and a file extension; three directory-only paths were
  corrected to the planned module paths before finalising). Key Files are
  consistent with the scope of each item.
- **Sequencing & dependencies review** — dependency graph is acyclic and
  matches the narrative ordering; the test item precedes the implementation
  item; docs follow the implemented behaviour; validation follows everything.
- **Scope sizing review** — each child is one session's worth of work (largest
  is item 3); no child bundles unrelated concerns; no child is a placeholder.
- **Acceptance & testability review** — every AC is pass/fail and names its
  verification (test module, report field, grep, `git diff --stat`, store
  read-back, full-suite run). Vague criteria were rewritten to name the
  observable evidence.
- **Polish & handoff review** — descriptions are copy-pasteable, UK English
  throughout, each names its worktree/build/test/commit expectations and
  records the commit hash on itself and on the parent.

## AC coverage review

`apply_coverage_review(SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H)` → `action: proceed`,
`created_children: []`, `conflicts: []`. All five parent ACs are covered by the
six children (mapping in the review notes above).

## Assumptions recorded for the producer (non-blocking)

1. **Design choice is delegated.** The parent says the implement phase may
   choose between designs A/B/C; item 1 makes that choice explicit and
   auditable. The plan's working assumption (not a requirement) is
   verify-then-transition (design A), because it adds no agent-facing step that
   a session can forget and keeps the existing finish lock and read-back
   assertion intact.
2. **Deferred worktree removal is driver-/caller-owned.** When `finish` defers
   worktree removal (driven child session, `--keep-worktree`), that cleanup is
   not a remaining implement-run step: the tree is the session's own cwd and
   ownership has passed to the driver/caller. Item 3 must document this
   explicitly (AC4 scope note) — it is not a hole in parent AC1.
3. **Post-push verification is a read-only cache check.** Moving it inside
   `finish` re-orders work; it must not start a suite run (parent risk

4. **No docs site exists in this repository.** Parent AC4's "wiki or docs site"
   maps to `docs/dev/*.md` plus the skill `SKILL.md` files; `CHANGELOG.md` stays
   with the ship pipeline.
5. **The audit-candidate predicate is external.** ContextHub's

## Full-suite red at 90c5b5da9 — 40 failures, dominated by shared-state pollution between concurrent agent test runs

Observed during the dev-push gate for SA-0MVQ6OXOA003RQFU (worktree `wl-SA-0MVQ6OXOA003RQFU-lane-a-clean-room-single-item-audit-re`, commit `90c5b5da9`). The change under test adds one audit test file, one log fixture and a docs section, so it cannot affect any of these suites; the changed-scope gate for it is green.

Failure groups (40 tests):

- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_claim.py` (4), `test_implement_extension.py` (2), `test_implement_submodules.py` (1), `test_implement_code_freeze_gate.py` (2) — all fail with `Work item SA-TEST is held by implement@pid <n> (session <id>)`. `phase_start` writes a **real** per-child lock file under `<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/child-SA-TEST.lock` for the synthetic id `SA-TEST`, so concurrent pytest processes see each other's leaked locks. Evidence: `.worklog/locks/child-SA-TEST.lock` currently holds `{"agent": "implement", "pid": 550428, "session_id": "herdr-1793412802-636939-32308", ...}` after that process exited.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_*` (10) — `phase_finish` reaches `run_gate_suite` and fails there (no free test slot / gate infrastructure), not on the assertion under test.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_plan_intake_integration.py` (7), `tests/test_effort_and_risk_e2e_status.py` (3), `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_fresh_repo_e2e.py` (2) — `wl init`/`wl` subprocess assertions under host load.
- `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` (6) — author-gate decision assertions failing in the same run.
- `tests/test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py`, `test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`, `test_validate_fanout.py` — one each (ingress/gate infrastructure).

Context: the host was running several other agents' full suites simultaneously (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2`, load average 8–14), which is also why the gate repeatedly reported `no free slot` and why the dev-push hook exceeded its 2700 s timeout.

Reproduce on a quiet host: `run_tests.py --scope full --json` from the commit above. If it is green when run alone, the fix is test isolation (per-test lock directory / `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`-style override for `.worklog/locks`) plus honest slot-contention reporting, not a code change in the failing suites.
